title: Scaling your startup: sales hiring, compensation and process, from Jason Calacanis and Launch
summary: Episode 5 of the Launch scaling series covers early sales. Founders run the first calls themselves, then hire a line account executive instead of a senior VP. Pay is roughly half base and half commission, paid when cash arrives. Other topics include outsourced SDRs, email sequences, BANT, and upselling.

principles.text: Founders should run the first sales calls themselves. A senior sales hire too early is set up to fail.
principles.quote: founders should be on those first sales calls they should do them themselves and it's very dangerous to hire somebody to senior

principles.text: Pair the founder with a line account executive and push for ~10 calls a week to learn objections and who buys.
principles.quote: just try to get ten phone calls under your belt every week and after five six seven you know weeks of that you're gonna be a really good shape to understanding what the objections are

principles.text: Treat first-year sales pay as half market research, half selling, since early deals are slow and inefficient.
principles.quote: I like to really think about their compensation half research and half actual selling

principles.text: Pay commission only when money comes in, so cancellations and refunds claw back and incentives stay honest.
principles.quote: I like people to get paid when the money comes in the door

principles.text: A rep who wants little variable pay is a bad sign. Aim for about 50/50 base and commission.
principles.quote: A red flag is somebody who wants less than a third of their compensation to come from commissions

principles.text: Great sales funds the fixes for everything else, so invest in the sales process early.
principles.quote: sell solves everything if you have great sales and you're selling boy every other problem seems to get solved because you have resources to go solve them
